senses.gloss: m.(b. h.; prob. fr. כבש to be thick, strong; cmp. Arab. kabš, a. v. אִימַּר) sheep (at least one year old).
units: <cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 13:7">Men. XIII, 7</cite>, sq.; a. fr.—Pl. <he>כְּבָשִׂים</he>.
<cite ref="Mishnah Menachot 13:9">Ib. 9</cite> <he>אחד מִכְּבָשַׂי</he> one of my sheep.
Zeb. IX, 5; a. fr.—Fem. כִּבְשָׂה or כַּבְשָׂה.
<cite ref="Bereishit Rabbah 44">Gen. R. s. 44</cite> <he>כ׳ של יחיד</he> the sheep which is offered as an individual’s sacrifice.
<cite ref="Tosefta Yevamot 3:4">Tosef. Yeb. III, 4</cite>; <cite ref="Yoma 66b:10">Yoma 66ᵇ</cite> (v. Tosaf. a. l.)—

<cite ref="Vayikra Rabbah 37">Lev. R. s. 37</cite>; Tanḥ. Vayishl. 8 <he>מביא</he> (<he>אדם</he>) <he>כִּבְשָׂתוֹ וכ׳</he> let man bring his sheep directly to the Temple court (without previous dedication by a vow); <cite ref="Jerusalem Talmud Nedarim 1:1:13">Y. Ned. I, 36ᵈ</cite> <he>כִּשְׂבָּתוֹ</he>. Tanḥ. Tol’d. 5; <cite ref="Esther Rabbah 10:11">Esth. R. to IX, 2</cite> <he>גדולה היא הכ׳ וכ׳</he> great is the sheep (Israel) that lives among seventy wolves (nations). Tanḥ. Ki Thissa 4 <he>אדם ששבה את הכ׳ וכ׳</he> a man who captured the lamb (Bathsheba, v.
<cite ref="II Samuel 12:3">II Sam. XII, 3</cite>, sq.) and killed the shepherd (Uriah); a. fr.
